about: I build AI agents and measure whether they actually work. This summer at 3E I took agent memory from an open research question to a working multi-tenant MCP service, and built the benchmark that shaped its design.

Before that I was a founding engineer at Euler AI, where I shipped a shopping assistant and an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline that measured hallucination across the product. My first-author paper, EvoRank, was presented at a RecSys 2026 workshop.
I'm finishing an M.S. in Applied Machine Learning at the University of Maryland. From June 2027 I want to work full-time on a team that takes agents, evals and ML systems to production.

principles.title: Prove the measurement before trusting the result
principles.body: At 3E I calibrated the LLM judge against blinded human graders before reading a single score. The rubric, not the judge model, turned out to be the accuracy lever. EvoRank gates the search with a pre-spend headroom check and re-scores every winner on held-out queries.

principles.title: The harness is part of the latency budget
principles.body: My on-device agent answered in 217 ms with a bare prompt and 3.9 to 4.5 s once about 935 tokens of system prompt and tool schemas were loaded. I traced it to CPU prefill. Tool definitions are not free.

principles.title: Let the model handle language and let code make the decisions
principles.body: In MedBill the model reads the bill, but a deterministic gate decides whether a No Surprises Act claim stands. In the SDS agent the model extracts, and CAS check-digit math verifies. The check digit doesn't hallucinate.

experience.summary: Took the agent-memory question from open research to a working MCP service in ten weeks, for a production compliance-AI platform.
highlights: Built the platform's only cross-system scoreboard for agent memory, comparing four existing memory systems (Hindsight, Cognee, Zep and AgentCore Memory) on the LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks, with byte-identical prompts and sha-pinned question sets so runs stay comparable.
Calibrated the LLM judge against blinded human graders and constructed ground truth before trusting its scores. The rubric, not the judge model, was the accuracy lever.
Wrote the architecture proposal from the results. The systems tied on easy recall but split on temporal reasoning, so the design routes by use case behind one API contract.
Implemented the core of the multi-tenant memory MCP service on AWS Lambda and DynamoDB: six operations, tenant access that denies by default, versioned writes and about 125 conformance tests.
Built a 120+ model capability catalog with live probes for the company's internal AI gateway.

details.findings_in_plain_words: On easy recall the memory systems tie, so the backend choice is a cost decision. On temporal reasoning it is an accuracy decision, so route by use case behind one contract. Abstention often moves opposite to accuracy. Stored extracted observations beat raw logs, which beat summaries. If a frozen index plus a good retriever could pass a memory test, the test measured retrieval, not memory.
details.how_he_works: Frozen spec as the contract, guard tests written to fail first, verification against the live deployment before calling anything done, and documents that cite their evidence.
details.other_work: In his first week he built and citation-audited a 98-paper literature corpus on agent memory. He also de-risked the serverless design with an MCP-on-Lambda spike validated by a 12-check acceptance suite against the live function.
details.how_he_got_it: He built two public prototypes of the company's own problem space (RegSentinel and SDS Intake Agent) before applying. The offer followed.
details.after: 3E offered him a part-time continuation for fall 2026.
details.what_not_to_say: The specific benchmark scores are internal to 3E. Hindsight, Cognee, Zep and AgentCore Memory are existing memory systems made by others; he benchmarked them, he did not build them. The memory service he built runs on Lambda and DynamoDB, and AgentCore was not its platform. Never describe security issues or vulnerabilities found at 3E or any employer; say only that he built tenant access that denies by default.

publications.title: EvoRank: LLM-Guided Evolution of Multi-Objective Learning-to-Rank Pipelines
publications.authors: Rayhan Patel and Shabaz Patel (equal contribution)
publications.summary: An LLM evolves complete learning-to-rank pipelines (features, models, losses, ensembles) for multi-objective hotel search. The contribution is the audit: a pre-spend headroom gate and a transfer audit on held-out queries.
publications.result: All three runs beat an Optuna-tuned LambdaMART on relevance (best +0.0057 NDCG@10, p < 0.0001, 59,902 held-out queries), and the best run beat it on every objective. A one-shot late submission would have placed 20th of 340 on the original Kaggle test set.

details.negative_result: The first campaign, which evolved only the training objective, selected noise: gains on the selection fold vanished on held-out data (+0.0002, p = 0.76) because the effects sat below the fitness fold's noise floor. Widening the search to whole pipelines cleared that floor.
details.leakage_story: Building the headroom gate surfaced three target-encoding leakage bugs. Leave-one-out encoding, the textbook fix, was worse than the naive version. Only out-of-fold encoding split by query was clean.
details.cost: About 50 iterations and about $10 of LLM spend per run.
details.presented: Presented as a poster on Sep 28, 2026 at RecSys 2026 in Minneapolis.
details.precise_claim: Significantly better relevance and conversion at matching revenue. Revenue was positive but inside the noise band.

publications.title: Building Domain-Specific LLMs Faithful to the Islamic Worldview: Mirage or Technical Possibility?
publications.authors: Shabaz Patel, Hassan Kane, Rayhan Patel
publications.summary: Tested whether prompting, RAG over 54K hadith, or GPT-3.5 fine-tuning makes LLMs answer faithfully to scholar answers. Built the evaluation (BERTScore and embedding distance) and presented the paper.
publications.result: Few-shot prompting was the most reliable across models. Fine-tuning on hadith plus IslamQA gave the best F1 (0.402).

projects.title: Production Chat Agent
projects.subtitle: The agent you can talk to on this site
projects.summary: A FastAPI and React agent that answers questions about my work. It streams over SSE, gates off-topic questions before the expensive call, reads a pasted job post, and keeps chatting when memory, database or tracing are down.
metrics: 95 tests, golden eval on every backend push
highlights: Every sentence of an answer is stamped checked, inferred or unknown: a fast model proposes a verbatim profile quote, code confirms it and checks every number. First run: 52 claims, 83% checked verbatim, none unknown.
Replaced Google's SDK with raw async HTTP/2 after it hung the server, and traced a silent production hang to a cache deadlock by bisecting with diagnostic endpoints.

Oct 2026: found it had been silently down for months (retired model, closed billing); wrote the post-mortem, made model IDs configuration, added a health probe that makes a real call, a fallback model, signed sessions, quotas and an MCP interface.

details.architecture: Frontend on Vercel behind Cloudflare. Backend on Railway, called directly so long streams avoid proxy timeouts. Thin route handlers delegate to services, and every external dependency (Supabase, Langfuse, the decision model) has an enabled flag so the chat degrades instead of failing.
details.models: Answers come from Gemini 3.5 Flash on Vertex AI, with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite as the fallback; Flash-Lite also classifies intent and parses job posts. Model IDs are configuration, because Google retires them.
details.security: SSRF-protected job URL fetcher, Cloudflare Turnstile, HTML stripped from every input, constant-time admin auth, and job descriptions fenced off as data so they can't override instructions.
details.bugs_worth_telling: A threading.Lock plus overridden dict methods deadlocked every POST endpoint with no errors and no logs. He built diagnostic endpoints to binary-search it, and the fix was one line. Separately, asyncio.wait_for hung on clients that ignore cancellation, so he wrote a timeout helper on asyncio.wait.
details.data: Its knowledge comes from the same profile file that renders rayhanpatel.com, so the site and the agent can't drift apart.
details.verification: Answers stream first; then a verification pass stamps each sentence (checked, inferred, unknown) with the profile quote it rests on, shown under the answer. Numbers that are not in the profile are flagged.
details.mcp: The same agent is exposed over MCP (read-only tools: get_profile, ask with stamps, fit_report) so other agents can call it; the web chat is one client of it.

projects.title: mcp-trust-monitor
projects.subtitle: Open-source guard for MCP tool calls
projects.summary: A Python SDK and CLI that holds an agent's MCP tool calls when a server's tool definitions change, until an operator approves the new revision.
highlights: Protected calls check approval, current metadata, launch identity and session freshness before dispatch. A changed definition, failed observation or quarantine blocks the call.
Background monitoring, a local operator console and decision-record export for audits.

projects.title: HVAC Copilot
projects.subtitle: On-device voice and vision agent for AR glasses
projects.kind: YC × Cactus × DeepMind hackathon · team of 4
projects.summary: A field assistant for HVAC technicians running Gemma 4 E4B fully on-device. One runtime serves three clients: Chrome, iPhone Safari and Rokid AR glasses over WebRTC.
metrics: TTFT 217 ms bare vs 3.9–4.5 s loaded
highlights: Built the assistant runtime and a six-tool function-calling surface, with the on-device/online boundary enforced in the dispatcher, not just the prompt.
Wrote a streaming sanitizer for Gemma 4's three tool-call formats so raw tool syntax never reaches the user.
Profiled the latency end to end and traced the 4 s first token to CPU prefill of the system prompt and tool schemas.

details.his_part: The assistant runtime, tool dispatcher and six-tool contract, the voice pipeline for the glasses (Silero VAD, faster-whisper, Kokoro TTS), latency instrumentation and the FastAPI/WebSocket server. A teammate built the Rokid Android app.
details.latency: Decode about 17 tokens/s. The glasses path took about 20 s end to end, and the Gemma turn was the dominant hop.
details.what_not_to_say: No placement or prize is claimed for this hackathon.

projects.title: FunctionGemma Hybrid Router
projects.subtitle: 2nd place, Cactus × Google DeepMind hackathon
projects.summary: Routes function calls between FunctionGemma-270M on-device and Gemini Flash-Lite in the cloud, deciding before inference because the small model reports high confidence even when it's wrong.
highlights: Pre-routing difficulty scoring, a validation gate that catches hallucinated tool names, and deterministic argument extraction for the 270M model's broken integers.
Proved that on-device beats a perfect cloud answer once local F1 passes 0.48 under the contest's scoring, and built around that.

details.prize: 2nd place. The prize was $1,000 in Gemini API credits.
details.benchmark: 30-case benchmark (10 easy, 10 medium, 10 hard). He started from about 50% F1.
details.integrity: Some top teams reached 16 ms by regex-matching the benchmark's exact query strings. He built a router that generalizes instead.

projects.title: Auto-Eval3D
projects.subtitle: Winner, Best Scientific & Engineering Application
projects.summary: Scores whether a generated 3D world stays consistent across viewpoints: prompt to World Labs Marble world, four inside-out views, then structured multi-view reasoning in Gemini.
highlights: Built the inside-out WebGL camera rig and a three-phase reasoning prompt that flags Janus artifacts, warping, scale shifts and floating geometry.
After the win I re-audited the traces. The demo's 1/10 score was judging a badly placed camera, not a bad world, so I rewrote the capture rig.

projects.title: Top-K k-NN kernel for the Cerebras WSE-2
projects.subtitle: Take-home, written in CSL
projects.summary: A distributed Top-K nearest-neighbour kernel across a grid of processing elements on the wafer-scale engine simulator: vectorized distance compute, a bounded heap per element, then a merge.
highlights: 2.68× fewer cycles than my first correct version, with bit-identical results on all six cases.
Measured a radix-sort variant at +24% cycles and rejected it.

details.note: The repository is private because it contains Cerebras's challenge materials. His own source is available on request.

projects.title: LLM inference config tuning
projects.subtitle: An LLM agent that tunes vLLM serving configs
projects.summary: Multi-objective tuning of LLM serving: throughput, time to first token and time per output token. I designed and built the LLM-agent method, one of five compared head to head against Bayesian optimization on shared benchmark infrastructure.
highlights: Same quasi-random warm start as the Bayesian baselines, so the comparison is fair by construction. Then one model call per trial, seeing the full sorted benchmark history, proposes the next config.
Every LLM-proposed config passes type coercion, schema repair and a hallucinated-key guard before it reaches a GPU. Benchmarked on Slurm.

details.what_not_to_say: The headline throughput and latency gains in the report belong to a teammate's method, not his.
